As July comes to a close, I figured now was as good as any to discuss our July book, Candide by Voltaire. So what did everyone think? Favorite part? Least favorite part? Curious to hear what everyone thought.

Personally, I really enjoyed the book. I've never read anything by Voltaire and was surprised by how accessible it was. I mean classic adventure novel. Even if it was a parody. Actually Candide reminded me a lot of Barry Lyndon by Kubrick, but maybe that was just due to the similar setting and time period.

So what philosophy did Candide end up following? I mean he's clearly rejected his mentor's optimism (that seemed to have a bit of predestination to it, something I think is strengthened by the role of the Anabaptist) but at the same time he doesn't seem to buy into Martin's unbridled pessimism. I guess he sort of becomes pragmatic? Like pray for rain but dig a well while you do it. Or is he almost an existential humanist in the Sartre kind of way when at the end of the novel he remarks "we must cultivate our garden" A secondary thing I thought was interesting was Candide frequently being "banished from Eden" Unlike biblical Eden however, these are due to his ignorance rather than knowledge. Is that the purpose of El Dorado? What about his constant killing? If anything innocence/ignorance seemed to be worst possible crime.

If you want to present a well-structured paper at school or work, follow these 2 guidelines:

  1. Use an introduction paragraph at the beginning and a conclusion paragraph at the end, but write them after you've finished writing the whole paper.
  2. Use the SEER method in writing each of the body paragraphs. State the main point of the paragraph in the first sentence. Use an Example that proves or backs that point. Then Explain how said example matters. Finally, Restate the main point of the paragraph in light of your example and explanation in the last sentence.

This way your paper will be easily understandable for anyone even if they only read the intro paragraph, skim the body by reading the first and last sentences of each paragraph, and end with reading the conclusion.

I got mostly hiking and camping tips.

Hiking

  • The night before you leave, get a water bottle fill half way, close it, and lay it down on it's side. You now have a water bottle ice that will last you a while.

  • buy a thermos and carry ice in it.

  • Put your phone on airplane mode. If you don't, the phone's objective would be to find a signal, thus draining the battery and heating the phone up.

  • Going into a place with lots of foliage, wear high socks and loose bright and light cloths. Ticks like damp, shady, brushy, and leafy areas.

  • Carry a watch. Good to know the time.

Camping

  • Do a spider check before you go to sleep in your tent.

  • In relation to spiders and ticks in your tent. Keep your cloths zipped your bag to limit their hiding spots.

  • When camping, take what you need, not what you want. For example, you need a pair of hiking shoes. You don't need your overly expensive fashion boots (glamping).
